I contacted G-Solar for a quote to upgrade our existing solar system — both with and without batteries — and advised them of the upcoming roof maintenance. The quoting process was seamless and completed entirely online. Once I accepted the quote, G-Solar agreed to remove the old panels so the roof work could be done before we went on holidays, with the new system to be installed upon our return. They were very accommodating to this arrangement.The technicians arrived on the scheduled day and got straight to work. Chris and his team were punctual, polite, and exceptionally tidy — so much so that a friend who installed our hot water system later commented on how neat the inverter installation was. After the installation, Chris even took the time to help me set up the monitoring app on my phone, allowing me to easily track our electricity usage.

5-Stars: If your expectations are that your installer will turn up the day they say they will, and you'll be generating electricity from the sun at the end of that day, then I would say for 90% of people you'd give 5-stars.5-Stars: The electrician Josh did an excellent job in the switchboard. It was very clean, tidy and well cable managed which was backed up by the Ergon Energy field tech who commented on how good the job was when installing our feed-in tariff metre. Josh's communication was good (a bit short notice but better than nothing) and he was personable, happy to answer any questions and most importantly, great at what he does. The only improvement I'd suggest is setting the hot water timer to a time of day where it will actually use the solar. We have all our panels on the Western side due to a lot of trees on the East, so having the hot water (3.6kW) come on at 7am defeats the purpose of taking it off the overnight tariff as we don't generate a single kilowatt until 9:00am and we only achieve 5kW from 10:30am - 3:30pm.3-Stars: The panel installation was done by a troop of backpackers (which I don't have an issue with at all) but certainly their attention to detail left a bit to be desired. I collected a couple of brackets and steel zip ties out of the gutter, the panels had a fair few hand prints on them where they had been leaned on during installation (testament to solar panels that something so thin can handle that kind of weight being applied to it) and one of the panels had been scratched down the side then face of it. The wrong brackets were also used which I guess is cosmetic as they don't sit flush against the panel but they're still fixed down securely and it's not like they'd be blown off the roof.To be fair the electrician had not yet been up on the roof to inspect the work, so he may have collected all the brackets and ties in the gutter and pointed out the scratch, but the panel installers had already jumped in the ute and headed off, so they certainly weren't tidying up after themselves.The conduit in the ceiling space was run smack down the centre of the cavity which is quite annoying when you're trying to get through a tight space already. Again I suspect 90% of people would never know as they're probably not up in their ceilings, but running cabling off to the side and out of the way of the main crawl space is a much better way to do it.3-Stars: The communication was okay. The installation was booked for 7:30am then you get a call at 7:29am to say they'll be there at midday then at 2pm get a call to say they're running late (not exact times as it was installed 4 months ago but you get my point). Then the scratched panel is going to get replaced 'next week' but you keep getting 'notice to pay' emails before reaching out to clarify that it's hopefully okay that you're not planning on paying the remaining balance until that scratched panel gets replaced (which they were happy with) and it has been 3 weeks already so 'you'll get a call tomorrow' which ends up being a couple of days later. Not the end of the world as more importantly the communication was great with nice and friendly staff, but on punctuality I wouldn't rate 5-Stars.It was also a bit of effort to get Customer Access so I could enable the API for HomeAssistant integration, but we got there in the end.So overall 3-Stars but I suspect most people aren't on the roof or in their ceiling spaces or in the switchboard and instead just check the Solar.web app to see if they're making electricity or not and if that's what you're after then the friendly service will tick all your boxes.
